climate.overview_html: Climate Week NYC 2026 closed on September 27 as the Turkish COP31 Presidency unveiled three linked pre-Antalya mechanisms: the BRIDGE climate finance initiative with Ethiopia, Fiji, Indonesia, Pakistan and Uzbekistan as its first five pilot countries, a contested electrification pledge targeting 35% electricity share of total energy by 2035 but criticised for omitting a clean-power sourcing requirement, and the Antalya AI Pledge committing signatories to climate-aligned AI design and deployment. The physical backdrop is unchanged: NOAA’s September 2026 ENSO forecast places a greater-than-90% probability on a historically strong Super El Niño peaking October–December 2026, and Carbon Brief’s Q3 analysis finds 2026 tracking the second-warmest year on record at ~1.51°C above pre-industrial with a 92% probability that 2027 surpasses it at ~1.71°C.

items.source: COP31 Presidency / Carbon Pulse / ARY News
items.headline: COP31 Presidency Announces BRIDGE Climate Finance Initiative at Climate Week NYC September 24: Ethiopia, Fiji, Indonesia, Pakistan, Uzbekistan as Pilot Countries; UNDP Partnership; Sustainable Urban Resilience Financing Facility (SURFF) Co-Launched with ILBANK, UN-Habitat and World Bank
items.summary: The COP31 Presidency announced at Climate Week NYC on September 24 the launch of the BRIDGE (Building Resilience and Implementation of Developing country Goals in Economies) initiative, with Ethiopia, Fiji, Indonesia, Pakistan and Uzbekistan as the first five pilot countries. Delivered in partnership with UNDP, BRIDGE seeks to bridge the gap between countries' NDC ambitions and investment-ready project pipelines by strengthening national capacity and developing bankable climate projects. The Presidency also co-launched the Sustainable Urban Resilience Financing Facility (SURFF) with ILBANK, UN-Habitat and the World Bank, targeting climate-resilient urban infrastructure in developing and vulnerable countries. Experience from the pilot cohort will inform expansion to additional developing countries, Small Island Developing States and Least Developed Countries ahead of COP31 in Antalya in November.

items.headline: COP31 Electrification Pledge (September 22): Governments to Target 35% Electricity Share of Total Energy Consumption by 2035 — Draws Immediate Criticism for Leaving Out Clean Power Commitment; Critics Warn It Opens Door to New Gas Generation While Nominally Consistent with 1.5°C Pathways
items.summary: The voluntary COP31 electrification pledge released on September 22 commits signatory governments to increasing electricity's share of total energy consumption to 35% globally by 2035, in line with pathways consistent with keeping 1.5°C alive. However, it does not explicitly require that additional electricity come from clean or zero-carbon sources — an omission drawing immediate criticism from activists and analysts who argue the pledge leaves open the possibility of meeting the target via new gas generation. Carbon Pulse analysis identified the gap as a significant weakness ahead of Antalya negotiations on NDC ambition.

items.headline: COP31 Presidency Announces Antalya AI Pledge September 21: Political Commitment on How AI Is Designed, Powered, Deployed and Managed in Support of Climate Action; UN Climate Chief Warns Big Tech “On Thin Ice” Over Data Center Emissions
items.summary: The Turkish COP31 Presidency launched the Antalya AI Pledge on September 21 at Climate Week NYC — a political commitment on how AI is designed, procured, powered, deployed, measured and managed in support of climate action. The pledge follows UN Secretary-General Guterres' public warning that big technology companies are 'on thin ice' for using expanded low-carbon pledges to justify accelerating data centre construction, expanding overall emissions even as grid carbon intensity falls. Signatories must align AI procurement with national climate commitments and disclose energy and water use.

items.headline: NOAA September 2026 ENSO Forecast: Greater-Than-90% Probability of Historically Strong El Niño Peaking OND 2026; 75% Probability of ‘Historic’ Event-Level Intensity (2015–16 Tier); Niño 3.4 ~+3.6°C; Persistence Through MAM 2027
items.summary: NOAA's September 2026 experimental ENSO predictions from the SPEAR seasonal forecast model place a greater-than-90% probability on a very strong El Niño event during the October–December 2026 peak season, with a 75% probability of achieving historic intensity in the 2015–16 tier. The current Niño 3.4 weekly index stands at approximately +3.6°C. The September forecast indicates a slightly weaker peak than August but maintains very high confidence in an event of exceptional intensity. Strong-to-moderate El Niño conditions are forecast to persist through March–May 2027.

items.source: Climate Impact Lab / University of Chicago
items.headline: Climate Impact Lab: Super El Niño Projected to Drive 451,000 Excess Heat Deaths Worldwide June 2026–February 2027 — Nigeria 31,400 / Indonesia 19,300 / Sudan 17,600; Sahel Hardest-Hit Region; 239,000 Deaths in September 2026–February 2027 Window
items.summary: The Climate Impact Lab at the University of Chicago released a mortality projection on September 23 estimating that the current Super El Niño will drive approximately 451,000 excess heat-related deaths worldwide between June 2026 and February 2027 — over and above deaths expected in an average year. The methodology is peer-reviewed, based on dose-response relationships across 24,378 sub-national regions globally. Nigeria is the most exposed nation at 31,400 excess deaths, followed by Indonesia (19,300) and Sudan (17,600); Africa's Sahel is the worst-affected region. For the six-month window September 2026 through February 2027, the projection is 239,000 deaths (±11,000).

items.headline: Nepal PM at UNGA September 25: Glacier-Collapse Floods Are “Warning to World”; Proposes Himalaya Climate Resilience Mechanism (Nepal–India–China); WWA Compound-Crisis Attribution: ~1.5°C Human-Caused Warming Confirmed in Langtang Region; 1,453+ Dead / 5,745+ Missing
items.summary: Nepal's Prime Minister addressed UNGA on September 25, framing the August 26 Langtang Lirung glacier-collapse floods — which killed at least 1,453 people and left 5,745 missing — as a 'warning to the world.' He proposed a Himalaya Climate Resilience Mechanism for shared satellite data, glacial lake monitoring and joint early warning between Nepal, India and China. The speech was backed by a World Weather Attribution compound-crisis study confirming that July–August 2026 temperatures in the Langtang Lirung region were approximately 1.5°C above background due to human-caused climate change, contributing to permafrost thaw and slope instability preceding the collapse.

items.headline: Carbon Brief State of Climate Q3 2026 (September 25): 2026 Tracking Second-Warmest Year on Record at ~1.51°C Above Pre-Industrial; Super El Niño Drives 92% Probability 2027 Becomes Warmest Year at ~1.71°C; Jan–Aug 2026 Anomaly 0.25°C Above 2023 at Same Point
items.summary: Carbon Brief's quarterly state-of-climate analysis finds the January–August 2026 period tracking 1.51°C above the 1850–1900 pre-industrial baseline — approximately 0.25°C warmer than 2023 at the same point in the year. The analysis places a 92% probability on 2027 becoming the warmest year on record at a central estimate of 1.71°C above pre-industrial, reflecting the well-documented 4–8 month lag between El Niño SST peak and global-mean temperature response.

major_events.status: TYPHOON — 130 km/h maximum sustained winds; gusts to 160 km/h; 685 km NE of Itbayat, Batanes as of 0500 LST September 27; NNE movement 15 km/h; exiting Philippine Area of Responsibility Sunday afternoon; tracking toward sea south of Okinawa
major_events.impact: No Philippines landfall forecast; surf and gale advisories east of Taiwan and Ryukyu Islands; potential intensification over warm waters south of Japan before extratropical transition expected early next week

weather.overview_html: The dominant weather story on September 27 is Typhoon Queenie (Surigae / JTWC 25W), which upgraded from Severe Tropical Storm to Typhoon overnight September 26–27 with maximum sustained winds of 130 km/h and gusts to 160 km/h, now exiting the Philippine Area of Responsibility and heading toward the sea south of Okinawa. In the Atlantic, Tropical Depression Fay — the first Atlantic named storm since early August — has formed but is nearly post-tropical at 29.8°N, 43.9°W with 30-knot maximum winds and is forecast to dissipate within days; the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season remains without a single hurricane. On land, Singapore’s 24-hour PSI hit 130 (unhealthy) in central Singapore on September 27 as haze from Kalimantan and Sumatra fires persists, while EFFIS forecasts very extreme fire danger across southern France, northern Spain and Portugal through September 30.

items.headline: Typhoon Queenie (Surigae / JTWC 25W) UPDATED September 27 0500 LST: Upgraded to Typhoon Overnight — 130 km/h Sustained Winds / Gusts 160 km/h; 685 km NE of Itbayat, Batanes; NNE Track at 15 km/h; Exiting PAR Sunday Afternoon; Tracking Toward Sea South of Okinawa; No Philippines Landfall
items.summary: The September 27, 2026, 5 a.m. PAGASA bulletin confirmed Typhoon Queenie (international name Surigae, JTWC designation 25W) had achieved typhoon intensity overnight, with maximum sustained winds of 130 km/h near the centre and gusts to 160 km/h. The centre was located 685 km northeast of Itbayat, Batanes, tracking north-northeastward at 15 km/h. Queenie will accelerate northeastward upon exiting the Philippine Area of Responsibility and is forecast to pass south of mainland Japan, likely undergoing extratropical transition early next week. No Philippines landfall is forecast throughout the advisory period. This upgrade from Severe Tropical Storm to Typhoon represents a significant intensification over the prior 12-hour bulletin, driven by warm sea surface temperatures (29–30°C) and reduced vertical wind shear east of Taiwan.

items.headline: Tropical Depression Fay Atlantic — First Named Storm Since August; 30-Knot Winds at 29.8°N 43.9°W; Near-Post-Tropical as Vertical Wind Shear Strips Convection; 2026 Atlantic Hurricane Season Continues Without a Hurricane — Record for Latest-in-Season First Hurricane Approaches October 8
items.summary: Tropical Depression Fay is located at 29.8°N, 43.9°W in the open central Atlantic with maximum sustained winds of 30 knots as of 00:00 UTC September 27. The NHC advises that increasing vertical wind shear is displacing convection away from the exposed low-level centre, and the latest forecast depicts a near-steady system on the verge of becoming post-tropical within 24–48 hours. Fay regenerated after initially forming in mid-September, but intensity forecasts remain pessimistic. The 2026 Atlantic hurricane season extends its record as the latest-in-season without a first hurricane; the previous record was the 1914 season. Should the season complete without a hurricane, it would be only the third such season since 1851.

items.source: Malay Mail / NEA Singapore / Mongabay / Wikipedia
items.headline: SE Asia Wildfire Haze UPDATED September 27: Singapore PSI Hits 130 (Unhealthy, Central Region) from Kalimantan and Sumatra Fires; NEA Forecasts Moderate-to-Low-Unhealthy Range; >617,400 Hotspots Detected; ASEAN Level 3 Alert Ongoing; Smoke Expected Through October
items.summary: Singapore's National Environment Agency reported on September 27 that the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index reached 130 in central Singapore — in the unhealthy range — due to smoke haze from fires in Kalimantan and Sumatra. At 9 a.m., PSI ranged from 90 to 130 across different regions. The NEA attributed the resurgence to south-easterly and south-westerly winds channelling fire smoke from Borneo and Sumatra. The agency forecasts conditions will remain in the moderate-to-low-unhealthy range. The broader 2026 Southeast Asian haze crisis has been ongoing since August 1 across Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand, Singapore and Vietnam, driven by more than 617,400 fire hotspots in Indonesia — double the same-date count for 2019 — with CAMS projecting smoke to persist through October as Super El Niño suppresses the Indonesian wet-season onset.

items.headline: Nepal PM at UNGA: Glacier-Collapse Floods Are “Warning to World” — Proposes Himalaya Climate Resilience Mechanism (Nepal–India–China); WWA Compound-Crisis Report Confirms 1.5°C Human-Caused Warming Contributed to August 26 Langtang Slope Failure; 1,453+ Dead / 5,745+ Missing
items.summary: Nepal's Prime Minister addressed UNGA on September 25, calling the August 26 glacier-collapse disaster — which killed at least 1,453 people and left 5,745 missing across Nepal and Tibet — a 'warning to the world.' He proposed a Himalaya Climate Resilience Mechanism for shared satellite data, glacial lake monitoring and joint early warning between Nepal, India and China. Backed by a World Weather Attribution compound-crisis study confirming that approximately 1.5°C of human-caused warming in July–August 2026 in the Langtang Lirung region contributed to permafrost thaw and slope destabilisation preceding the collapse.

items.headline: Europe Wildfire EFFIS Update September 24: 678,978 ha Burned as of September 23 (91% Above 20-Year Average) — Very Extreme Fire Danger Forecast 24–30 September for Southern France, Northern Spain and Portugal; Below 2025 Record of 1,026,104 ha
items.summary: EFFIS data updated September 24 places total European area burned as of September 23 at 678,978 hectares — 91% above the 20-year average (2006–2025) of 355,397 ha. Ahead of EFFIS's next bulletin, very extreme fire danger anomalies are forecast for southern and central France, northern Spain and Portugal through September 30. The season remains below the record 1,026,104 ha burned by September 23, 2025, but sits well above long-term norms, driven by Super El Niño-amplified drought and record summer temperatures across southern and central Europe.

renewables.overview_html: WindEnergy Hamburg 2026 (September 22–25) produced two new turbine milestones: Vestas secured the first global order for its newly launched V182-7.2 MW turbine — a 29 MW Staverhult project in Sweden from SR Energy, with a 35-year AOM 5000 service agreement, while Nordex debuted the N193/7.X (193 m rotor, up to 7.3 MW), expanding its Delta4000 series with an up-to-14% energy yield gain over the N175/6.X at low-to-medium wind sites. On the grid side, the U.S. DOE SPARK initiative’s $5.25 billion in total investment across 31 projects in 26 states continues to unlock 23 GW without new transmission corridors, while Fluence’s 206 GWh multi-year EVE Energy supply framework through 2031 underscores accelerating BESS market confidence.

items.source: Renewable Energy Magazine / Renewables Now / Recharge
items.headline: Vestas Wins First Global Order for New V182-7.2 MW Onshore Turbine — SR Energy’s 29 MW Staverhult Wind Farm, Sweden; Launched September 21 at WindEnergy Hamburg; 35-Year AOM 5000 Service Agreement; Serial Production from End-2027; Delivery 2Q28
items.summary: Vestas secured the first commercial order for its newly launched V182-7.2 MW turbine just one day after the turbine's official market launch on September 21. SR Energy ordered four V182-7.2 MW units for the 29 MW Staverhult wind farm in southern Sweden, including a 35-year Active Output Management 5000 (AOM 5000) service agreement. The V182-7.2 MW builds on Vestas's proven EnVentus platform. Serial production is set to begin from end-2027, with turbine delivery expected in 2Q28 and commissioning in 3Q28.

items.headline: Nordex Debuts N193/7.X at WindEnergy Hamburg September 22: 193 m Rotor / Up to 7.3 MW; 95 m Single-Piece Blades; Up-to-14% Energy Yield Gain vs. N175/6.X at Low-to-Medium Wind Sites; German-Market 6.6 MW Cap; Series Production 2029
items.summary: Nordex unveiled the N193/7.X on September 22 at WindEnergy Hamburg, expanding its Delta4000 series with a 193-metre rotor diameter, 95-metre single-piece blades and a rated capacity of up to 7.3 MW. The turbine is designed for medium- and low-wind sites and can increase energy yield by up to 14% compared with the N175/6.X. For the German market, a maximum capacity of 6.6 MW applies. Key components — nacelle, turbine control system, electrical architecture — are retained and optimised from the established Delta4000 platform, leveraging existing production and logistics. Series production is scheduled to start in 2029.

items.source: U.S. Department of Energy / TD World
items.headline: DOE Announces $1.9 Billion Federal Funding ($5.25 Billion Total with Cost-Share) for 31 Grid-Improvement Projects Across 26 States Under SPARK Initiative — 1,500+ Miles Reconductored; 23 GW Capacity Unlocked; 21,000 Miles of Grid-Enhancing Technology Deployment
items.summary: The U.S. Department of Energy's Office of Electricity announced on September 24, 2026 the selection of 31 grid-improvement projects across 26 states under the SPARK initiative. $1.9 billion in federal funding plus $3.35 billion in recipient cost-share brings total investment to $5.25 billion. Projects will reconductor or rebuild more than 1,500 miles of transmission lines and deploy Grid-Enhancing Technologies across nearly 21,000 miles of existing lines, unlocking more than 23 GW of additional capacity for roughly 100 million Americans without building new transmission corridors. Formal financial-assistance agreements are expected between October 2026 and January 2027.

items.headline: Fluence — EVE Energy 206 GWh Multi-Year Battery Supply Framework 2027–2031 — Utility-Scale BESS Systems; EVE-3 Cylindrical Cell Technology; One of Largest Long-Term BESS Supply Commitments in Industry
items.summary: Fluence announced on September 24 a multi-year battery supply framework agreement with EVE Energy covering 206 GWh of utility-scale battery energy storage systems from 2027 through 2031, deploying EVE's new EVE-3 large-format cylindrical cell technology in Fluence's Gridstack and Ultrastack BESS platforms. The 206 GWh five-year commitment covers approximately 5 GW of estimated projects and is one of the largest long-term BESS supply frameworks in the utility-scale storage industry.

items.headline: RWE at WindEnergy Hamburg September 22: Calls for Europe-Wide CfD Indexation for Offshore Wind; Up to €4.4 Billion in Savings for Germany’s 9 GW Pipeline by 2030; €2 Billion Savings for 4 GW Tendered in 2027
items.summary: RWE's head of offshore wind development called at WindEnergy Hamburg on September 22 for Europe-wide adoption of inflation indexation for offshore wind Contracts for Difference, linking strike prices to inflation indices over the operating term. For Germany's 4 GW planned for tendering in 2027, potential cost reductions are estimated at up to €2 billion; for Germany's full 9 GW tender pipeline through 2030, up to €4.4 billion.

items.headline: CTUIL Releases TSA for 2 GW Solapur Renewable Energy Evacuation and Transmission Expansion Project (India) — 10-Day Window to Execute and Acquire 100% SPV Equity; Part of India’s 500 GW Renewable Target Grid Reinforcement
items.summary: Central Transmission Utility of India Ltd (CTUIL) released a Transmission Service Agreement on September 23 for a 2 GW renewable energy evacuation and transmission expansion project in Solapur, Maharashtra. The selected bidder has 10 days to execute the TSA and acquire 100% equity in the Special Purpose Vehicle. The project is part of India's grid reinforcement program to evacuate power from the Solapur solar and wind zones — a critical bottleneck for India's 500 GW renewable target by 2030.

science.overview_html: Three additions this cycle: Stochastically Perturbed Weights (SPW) tests ensemble generation from four deterministic ML weather-model checkpoints (Aurora, GraphCast, SFNO, AIFS) at zero marginal training cost, reaching CRPSS 0.04–0.13 below trained-probabilistic baselines at 10 days; Hess et al. demonstrate up to 19% CRPS improvement by fine-tuning a graph-transformer weather model directly on IMERG satellite precipitation data rather than ERA5; and ECMWF’s September 24 AI Weather Quest annual highlights webinar concluded the competition’s first year and announced continuation as a long-term sub-seasonal ML benchmarking framework. The most operationally significant carried finding remains the Landsberg & Barnes (GRL, September 24) identification of a 15–20-year cold bias (~0.035°C/decade) inherited from ERA5 training data in AIFS, GraphCast and Pangu-Weather 2-m temperature forecasts.

items.headline: Stochastically Perturbed Weights (arXiv:2609.08412): Ensembles from Deterministic ML Weather Models at Zero Marginal Training Cost — Aurora, GraphCast, SFNO, AIFS Benchmarked; CRPSS 0.04–0.13 Below Trained-Probabilistic Baseline at 240-Hour Lead; Architecture-Specific Tensor Groups Required
items.summary: Stochastically Perturbed Weights (SPW) asks how much ensemble spread can be extracted from a deterministic ML weather model checkpoint without retraining. The authors perturb the network's raw weight tensors at inference time — analogous to stochastically perturbed parameterisation tendencies in NWP ensemble systems — and benchmark the resulting ensembles across four deterministic backbones: Aurora, GraphCast, SFNO and AIFS. At 240-hour (10-day) lead time, SPW ensembles reach CRPSS 0.04–0.13 below the best trained-probabilistic baseline at zero marginal training cost. However, no single injection site works across all architectures — the productive tensor group is model-specific — making SPW currently a tuning procedure rather than a plug-and-play recipe. Practically significant for energy and climate-risk teams running commercial ML weather models without access to training infrastructure.

items.headline: Improving Precipitation Forecasts in AI Weather Models Using Observational Data (arXiv:2609.03210): IMERG Fine-Tuning of Graph-Transformer at 0.25° Improves Medium-Range CRPS Up to 19%; Superior Skill for Tropical Storms and Drizzle; Challenges of ERA5 Precipitation Bias Directly Addressed
items.meta: Hess et al. · arXiv:2609.03210 [cs.LG] · Submitted September 2026
items.summary: Hess et al. demonstrate that AI weather prediction models trained exclusively on ERA5 carry systematic precipitation biases, particularly for convective events and drizzle, and that these can be substantially reduced by fine-tuning on observational data. They fine-tune a graph-transformer architecture with NASA's IMERG satellite precipitation product at 0.25° resolution, producing up to 19% improvement in medium-range continuous ranked probability scores. The fine-tuned model also shows superior tropical storm precipitation skill and better drizzle event representation. The approach is broadly applicable to other reanalysis-trained ML weather models suffering ERA5 precipitation bias.

items.headline: ECMWF AI Weather Quest Annual Highlights Webinar September 24: First-Year Rankings Awarded; Leading Teams from China, Europe and US Present Approaches; Competition Announced as Long-Term International Sub-Seasonal ML Benchmarking Framework in Partnership with WMO
items.summary: ECMWF hosted the AI Weather Quest annual highlights webinar on September 24, 2026, in collaboration with WMO as part of the WMO AI Webinar series, celebrating the first year of the competition. Leading teams from China, Europe and the United States presented their approaches and lessons learned from developing real-time weekly sub-seasonal ML forecasts across four 13-week competition periods from August 2025 to September 2026. ECMWF announced the competition's continuation as a long-term international benchmarking and learning framework, positioning the Quest as a community resource for advancing probabilistic sub-seasonal AI weather prediction beyond the medium range.

items.headline: Lightweight Probabilistic Downscaling from a Deterministic Base Model (arXiv:2609.29383) — Two-Stage Curriculum (Deterministic Pretraining + Probabilistic Tuning) on U-Net Backbone; Beats State-of-the-Art RMSE on CORDEX-ML-Bench (Alps, NZ, South Africa); Daily Tmax and Precipitation
items.meta: McLean, Vlaar, Passano Hellan, Ericsson · arXiv:2609.29383 [cs.LG] · Submitted 24 September 2026
items.summary: McLean et al. introduce a lightweight probabilistic climate downscaling approach built on a modified U-Net backbone trained with a two-stage curriculum combining deterministic pretraining with probabilistic tuning. Evaluated on the CORDEX-ML-Bench suite for daily maximum temperature and precipitation across three geographic regions — the Alps, New Zealand and South Africa — the approach beats state-of-the-art RMSE while remaining computationally accessible. The result reduces the trade-off between computational intensity and distributional fit that has constrained probabilistic downscaling at high resolution.

items.source: Geophysical Research Letters / AGU / Colorado State University
items.headline: GRL: AI Weather Model 2-m Temperature Forecasts Carry 15–20-Year Cold Bias From ERA5 Training Data — Landsberg & Barnes (CSU); ~0.035°C/Decade Systematic Underestimate in ECMWF AIFS, GraphCast, Pangu-Weather; Bias Correction Required Before Climate Attribution
items.meta: Landsberg & Barnes · Colorado State University · Geophysical Research Letters (2026) · Published 24 September 2026
items.summary: Landsberg and Barnes evaluate 2-metre temperature forecasts from ECMWF AIFS, Google DeepMind GraphCast and Huawei Pangu-Weather, identifying a systematic cold bias of approximately 0.035°C per decade inherited from the ERA5 reanalysis training corpus. All three models show consistent negative temperature bias growing with forecast lead time. The study concludes these models are unsuitable for near-real-time climate attribution without explicit post-processing bias correction and calls for training dataset refreshes or dynamic climatology normalisation as standard practice.

items.headline: HClimRep-Ocean (arXiv:2609.28601) — First Transformer Ocean Emulator on FESOM2 Unstructured Mesh; Full 3D Reconstruction Including Sea Ice, Salinity, SSH; State-of-the-Art vs. ClimaX and FourCastNet Ocean Baselines at 1–12-Month Horizons
items.summary: HClimRep-Ocean introduces the first transformer-based ocean emulator operating on FESOM2's native unstructured triangular mesh, avoiding regridding artifacts. Variables include 3D temperature and salinity at 24 depth levels, sea surface height, and sea ice concentration and thickness. The model achieves state-of-the-art skill versus ClimaX ocean fine-tune and FourCastNet ocean baselines across all variables at 1–12-month prediction horizons. The unstructured-mesh capability is particularly significant for accurately representing coastal upwelling zones and polar ocean processes.

items.headline: FAST-ML (arXiv:2609.25505) — Hybrid Physics–ML Framework for Tropical Cyclone Intensity Forecasting; Dual-Stream ERA5 Neural Parameterization Coupled to Differentiable FAST Intensity Model; End-to-End Optimization for Rapid Intensification
items.meta: Xiao, Lin, Ehrmann, Sarhadi · arXiv:2609.25505 [physics.ao-ph] · Submitted 22 September 2026
items.summary: FAST-ML bridges data-driven efficiency with physical constraints for tropical cyclone intensity forecasting, targeting rapid intensification. A physically-informed dual-stream neural parameterization ingests 3D ERA5 atmospheric fields to diagnose ventilation controls fed into a differentiable implementation of the FAST intensity model with end-to-end optimization. Relevant to Typhoon Queenie (25W) intensity guidance as it approaches Japan.

items.headline: Transfer Learning for Atmospheric Transport Emulators (arXiv:2609.23838) — Clark et al. (U Bristol); LPDM Emulator Extended from South America to Four Global Regions; ~1,000× Faster Than Physics-Based Model; Enables High-Resolution Satellite GHG Inversion at Scale
items.meta: Clark, Fillola, Keshtmand, Santos-Rodriguez, Rigby · arXiv:2609.23838 [physics.ao-ph] · Submitted 20 September 2026 · University of Bristol
items.summary: Evaluates whether a high-performance Lagrangian Particle Dispersion Model emulator — running approximately 1,000× faster than the UK Met Office's NAME LPDM — can be spatially transferred to new regions via transfer learning. Establishes conditions for extending the emulator without full retraining, opening a pathway toward global, high-resolution greenhouse gas inversion from modern satellite instruments (OCO-2, TROPOMI) at previously unaffordable computational cost.

items.headline: WeatherNext 3 (arXiv:2609.03582) — Google DeepMind: Operational Hourly Global Probabilistic Forecasts at 0.1° via Raw Geostationary Satellite Ingestion; Functional Generative Networks on Multiresolution Icosahedral Mesh; Powers Google Search + Google Maps
items.meta: Google DeepMind + Google Research · arXiv:2609.03582 [cs.LG] · Submitted 3 September 2026 · Operational
items.summary: WeatherNext 3 generates new probabilistic forecasts every hour by ingesting low-latency geostationary satellite imagery directly, achieving 0.1° spatial resolution while eliminating the 6-hour analysis lag that constrains traditional AI model architectures. Architecture: Functional Generative Networks on a multiresolution icosahedral mesh. Now operationally deployed by Google, powering weather data in Google Search and Google Maps.

items.title: Isometric (Carbon MRV / Industrial Certification) Extends Series A to €43 Million (~US$50 M) with Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) Backing — Round Led by AVP (AXA Venture Partners); AXA Anchor Investor; Platform Now Certified >16 Million Tonnes; Expanding Beyond Carbon Removal Into Industrial Emissions, Energy and Fuels
items.body_html: UK climate-tech startup Isometric extended its Series A to €43 million (~US$50 M) in September 2026, adding Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) and a cluster of corporate and sovereign investors — Dubai Future District Fund, Acario Innovation, BY Venture Partners, Earth VC, One Capital — to a round that initially priced at $40 M in June 2026. ICE’s participation is strategically significant: Isometric’s AI-driven certification platform — which has already certified more than 16 million tonnes of carbon removal — is now expanding into industrial emissions, energy and materials certification, directly relevant to ICE’s voluntary carbon market infrastructure. Total lifetime funding reaches approximately $75 M.

items.title: Juniper Re Licenses KatRisk Severe Convective Storm and Wildfire Catastrophe Models — Expands Existing Flood Model Relationship; Covers Hail, Tornado and Straight-Line Wind; KatRisk Wildfire Model Co-Developed with Technosylva
items.body_html: Juniper Re licensed KatRisk’s Severe Convective Storm (SCS) and Wildfire catastrophe models on September 24, expanding an existing relationship that already included KatRisk’s flood modeling capabilities. The KatRisk SCS model provides a probabilistic view of hail, tornado and straight-line wind risk across the United States. The KatRisk Wildfire Model was co-developed with Technosylva and models the physical ignition and fire-spread processes — two perils where traditional cat models have faced significant challenges reproducing post-2020 loss experience including the 2026 European wildfire season.

items.title: Climate Proof “State of Adaptech Investing H1 2026”: 80 Deals (+84% YoY Capital to US$1.29 Billion); Average Deal Size $20.9 M (2× Year-Ago); Earth Observation and Weather Forecasting Drive Supersized Rounds; Nature-Based Solutions Capital Down to Under 6% of Total
items.body_html: Climate Proof’s State of Adaptech Investing H1 2026 report finds that climate adaptation technology companies raised US$1.29 billion in the first half of 2026 — up 22% from H2 2025 and 84% year-on-year — across 80 disclosed deals, a decline from prior periods reflecting a bifurcation toward fewer but larger rounds. Average disclosed deal size jumped to US$20.9 M, more than double the year-ago half, driven by supersized later-stage equity raises in Earth Observation and Weather Forecasting solution areas, while nature- and biodiversity-focused adaptation capital collapsed from 25% of all adaptech investment in H1 2025 to under 6% in H1 2026.

items.title: DOE SPARK Initiative Selects 31 US Grid Projects for $1.9 Billion Federal Funding ($5.25 Billion Total with Cost-Share) — 1,500+ Miles Reconductored; 23 GW Unlocked Without New Corridors; 21,000 Miles of Grid-Enhancing Technology Deployment Across 26 States
items.body_html: The U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of Electricity announced on September 24 the selection of 31 grid-improvement projects across 26 states under the SPARK initiative, with $1.9 billion in federal funding and $3.35 billion in recipient cost-share for a total of $5.25 billion. Projects will reconductor or rebuild more than 1,500 miles of transmission lines and deploy Grid-Enhancing Technologies across nearly 21,000 miles of existing lines, unlocking more than 23 GW without new corridors; formal financial-assistance agreements are expected between October 2026 and January 2027.

items.title: Fortune / PitchBook: Climate Tech VC Fund Fundraising Fell ~40% in H1 2026 Despite Record Investment Totals — AI Data Centre Demand Filling Gap Left by Pure-Climate Funds; Bifurcation Sharpening Between AI-Adjacent and Traditional Climate-Only Verticals
items.body_html: Fortune, citing PitchBook LP fundraising data, reported on September 23 that climate-tech-dedicated VC fund formation fell approximately 40% in H1 2026 by capital raised compared to H1 2025 — even as total climate-tech investment reached a record $26.1 billion in the same period. The paradox reflects AI-infrastructure demand for firm low-carbon power being increasingly funded by generalist and growth funds that do not self-identify as “climate VC.” PitchBook’s analysis finds the 10 largest H1 2026 climate deals drew on sovereign wealth funds, Big Tech corporate VC and pension capital — potentially hollowing out the early-stage climate pipeline if LPs continue to withdraw from pure-play climate fund vehicles.

items.title: Kairos Power Secures Up to $100 Million from Samsung C&T for Google Hermes 2 Nuclear Reactor Build — $70 M Equity + $30 M In-Kind Engineering; 50 MW Fluoride Salt-Cooled Demonstration Plant at Oak Ridge; Operations Target 2030
items.body_html: Kairos Power and Samsung C&T agreed on September 21 to a binding term sheet under which Samsung C&T will provide up to $100 million — $70 million equity plus $30 million in-kind engineering — to support the delivery of the 50 MW fluoride salt-cooled Hermes 2 Demonstration Plant in Oak Ridge, Tennessee. Hermes 2 is purpose-built to supply firm low-carbon baseload power for Google’s AI data centres; Samsung C&T brings direct reactor construction execution capability across approximately a dozen nuclear projects globally.
items.source_html: TechCrunch / World Nuclear News

items.title: Rainmaker Raises $100 Million Series B for Drone-Based Cloud Seeding — Led by NOA VC + Upfront; DCVC, Lowercarbon, Dream Ventures Co-Invest; Targets Drought Relief in American West and Data Center Water Demand
items.body_html: Rainmaker, the El Segundo weather-modification startup, announced a $100 million Series B on September 21 led by NOA VC and Upfront Ventures, with co-investment from DCVC, Lowercarbon Capital and Dream Ventures — bringing total funding to $150.3 million since its 2023 founding. Rainmaker deploys drone fleets to seed clouds with silver iodide, targeting drought relief in the American West and humidification services for water-hungry hyperscale data centres.

items.title: CTVC / Currence H1’26 Climate Tech Report: $26.1 Billion Global VC in H1 2026 (+55% YoY); Data Centers 34% of Total; Deal Count at 5-Year Low (-25%); Series A up 55% to $4.5 Bn; Adaptation Funding +64% — Fastest-Growing Sub-Vertical
items.body_html: CTVC (now Currence) published its H1’26 Climate Tech Investment Report on September 21, finding total global venture investment reached $26.1 billion in H1 2026 — up 55% year-on-year — driven overwhelmingly by data-centre infrastructure. The Built Environment category grew more than 800% and overtook Energy as the largest funding vertical, with deal count falling 25% to a 5-year low; the 10 largest rounds taking 42% of all H1 2026 investment; Series A rising 55% to $4.5 billion; and adaptation funding growing 64% — the fastest-growing sub-vertical.

items.title: Cat Bond and ILS Market Bulletin (Week Ending September 20): MembersCap Launches First Cat Bond Fund + Novel ILW; Gallagher Securities Developing First-Ever New-Peril Cat Bond; CalPERS ILS Holdings Approach US$2.5 Billion; Record $11 Billion Q2 2026 Issuance; Artemis London 2026 Closes
items.body_html: The Artemis weekly bulletin for the week ending September 20 highlights: MembersCap launched the first dedicated cat bond fund strategy alongside a novel ILW structure; Gallagher Securities is developing the first-ever cat bond covering a previously unbondable peril; and CalPERS’ ILS holdings are approaching US$2.5 billion at mid-year 2026 — the fifth consecutive year of global insured nat-cat losses exceeding US$100 billion and Q2 2026 posting a record $11 billion in cat bond issuance. Artemis London 2026 also concluded this week with the consensus finding that the cat bond market is well-positioned for disciplined, continued growth.
